scope: Bounded Linux CPU comparisons of successive simplification snapshots against the implemented forward-autodiff baseline; not complete final-head qualification
baseline: Uncommitted forward-autodiff implementation before simplification; the baseline source is not the base commit. Per-report native and Python fingerprints identify the measured built package.
candidate: Three successive uncommitted simplification snapshots sharing one native binary and differing Python-package hashes; preserve each run boundary.
method: Every report compares separately built release packages in seven alternating paired rounds, with four threads pinned to CPUs 8-11, three samples per round and at least 20 ms per sample.
The ratio is the median of paired candidate/baseline ratios. The speed allowance is 1.05 for baseline calls of at least 1 ms and 1.10 below 1 ms; output agreement uses relative tolerance 1e-12.

The broad report contains 15 physics workflows, 12 JAX input-context microbenchmarks and two direct native Bessel cases. All 15 physics workflows passed their measured speed limits. Three JAX value-and-JVP cases failed in this earlier snapshot; those failures remain in the report.
The input_contexts report reran all 12 JAX microbenchmarks after reducing Python argument-binding overhead. Wigner value-and-JVP remained above its 10 percent allowance; the other 11 cases passed.

The wigner report reran three Wigner microbenchmarks after the final Wigner preparation simplification. Its value-and-JVP paired ratio is 1.11314720588728, an 11.3 percent slowdown; the difference between median call times is approximately 18.9 microseconds. Its failed verdict is retained.

Derivative-only JVP and gradient microbenchmarks improved by approximately 30-42 percent in the later runs. These savings and the combined value-and-JVP cost describe the sampled input-only contexts and JAX callback overhead, not a universal forward-mode speedup.

The later reports do not rerun the broad physics suite at their Python-source hashes. These snapshots are bounded regression evidence, not a claim that every case was qualified on the final PR head or on other platforms.
All recorded numerical fields, timing rounds, ratios, agreement results, failure flags and as-run fingerprints are archived unchanged. No measurement was rerun for publication.

diagnostic_driver.description: Temporary driver adding input-context cases to scripts/compare_builds.py. The benchmark_sha256 in all three reports identifies this driver, not compare_builds.py alone.
diagnostic_driver.replay_note: The archived source uses a repository-root placeholder. Set ROOT to a local checkout and provide separately built baseline/candidate package paths to rerun. Package source snapshots are identified by hashes and are not bundled in this report.

privacy: Private host labels and the incidental workspace path in the archived driver were replaced. Original report and driver hashes remain as-run facts; original and distributed artifact hashes are recorded in benchmarks/privacy-provenance.json.
